utility.notes: SCE's own 'Incorporated Cities and Counties Served by SCE' fact sheet (updated 3/17/2025) explicitly lists 'Lake Elsinore' by name among the cities in its service area. This is corroborated by search-engine indexing of the city's own site, which states Lake Elsinore homes are served by SCE.

value.name: Southern California Edison (SCE)
value.notes: Lake Elsinore was never a Western Community Energy member city (its member cities were Eastvale, Hemet, Jurupa Valley, Norco, Perris, and Wildomar), and WCE itself deregistered with the CPUC and dissolved via Chapter 9 bankruptcy in 2021 — so no CCA currently operates anywhere in Riverside County. SCE is recorded as both the distribution and generation utility.

permit_authority.value: City of Lake Elsinore Building & Safety Division

interconnection_url.notes: SCE's own Net Energy Metering (NEM) program page — a utility-wide fact already established for other SCE-territory records this session.

value.name: SGIP - Residential Solar and Storage Equity
value.administrator: Southern California Edison (SCE), under the CPUC's Self-Generation Incentive Program
value.description: Storage incentive of $1,100/kWh paired with a solar incentive of $3,100/kW, funded via a $280 million CPUC-authorized budget that opened for reservations June 2, 2025. Administered by SCE across its entire distribution territory, which includes Lake Elsinore/Riverside County.
value.eligibility: PG&E or SCE residential customers (general market tier)

battery_programs.notes: Same statewide CPUC-administered SGIP program already confirmed for other SCE-territory records this session, reused as a utility-level fact.

Electrical single-line diagram showing panel count/voltage/kW ratings, main panel bussing amperage, and PV circuit breaker amperage
Manufacturer's information brochures for the inverter, PV modules, and mounting system

required_documents.notes: Per the City's own 'Solar Requirements' handout (Building and Safety Department), condensed from the full itemized list.

value: Call the inspection line at 951-225-1818, providing the project address, permit number, inspection type, and a callback number
Calls received before 5:00pm on a workday are scheduled for the following workday; confirm you are on the inspection list by calling 951-674-3124 after 8:00am (inspectors do not call to confirm)
Inspections are not currently scheduled through the CSS Portal
inspection_steps.notes: This is the City's general Building & Safety inspection-scheduling process (the same page covers all building permit types, including solar); the City does not publish a separate, solar-specific inspection sequence.

value.notes: The City's own 'Solar Requirements' handout states: 'As of January 1, 2019 Permits for Solar Systems will no longer be issued over the counter, there will be a 1-3 day plan check review.'

value.program_or_pathway: Standard plan check review (1-3 days) per the City's Solar Requirements handout
other_conditions: 36-inch minimum clearance required at ridgeline, valleys, and eaves where arrays are installed on roofs; arrays may extend to the eave if 3 ground-to-ridge access points remain
Ground-mounted arrays require a minimum 10-foot vegetation clearance/mowed perimeter and may require Planning Department site plan approval
Total roof dead load (existing roof + array) exceeding 10 lbs/sq ft, or tile roofing/trussed roof, requires a structural analysis
